subject: Next steps: model shortlist + SLO traces for HealthWave pilot
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Jenkins <hannah.jenkins@healthwave.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Next steps: model shortlist + SLO traces for HealthWave pilot

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to learn more about HealthWave's triage and note-summarization workflow. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

Call highlights:
- Primary goal: improve triage recall and concise patient-note summaries with strict latency SLOs for EMR integration.
- Typical request size: ~600 tokens (avg), burst to 1,200 tokens during peak hours.
- Success metrics: clinical recall > 0.92 on our prompt set, p95 latency <= 250ms for 1–2 concurrent requests, target throughput ~40–60 TPS for batched inference.

Recommended model shortlist (opinionated):
1) RW-13B-quant (recommended starting point) — best balance of quality and 8-bit inference cost; see attached perf snapshot and SLO trace.
2) Redwood-3-small — lower-cost candidate for non-critical summarization paths (good for heavy batching).
3) LlamaX-7B-8bit — keep as fallback for extremely tight latency windows.

Attached: redwood_perf_snapshot_20261212.pdf (Redwood-verified perf profiles, throughput vs sequence length), healthwave_prompt_set_v1.txt (sample prompts we used for quick qual checks).

Quick numbers from the RW-13B-quant profile (95th percentile conditions, 1k token max):
- Sustained TPS (single-node, 80% load): ~45 TPS
- p50 latency: ~48 ms
- p95 latency: ~220 ms
- p99 latency: ~410 ms

Next steps I recommend:
1) We run a 2-week pilot (Redwood Dedicated or hosted sandbox) using your sample logs — need one sample dataset + estimated daily QPS.
2) Schedule a 30-minute technical deep-dive with our runtime team (Vivek + Ben suggested) to scope on-prem vs Dedicated requirements.
3) I'll share full benchmark links and a short SLO trace image; please confirm target p95 and whether on-prem estimate is required.

Proposed slots for the deep-dive: Tue 12/15 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 12/16 13:00–13:30 PT — tell us what works.

Thanks,

Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_perf_snapshot_20261212.pdf (pdf), healthwave_prompt_set_v1.txt (text)

From: Hannah Jenkins <hannah.jenkins@healthwave.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T16:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: model shortlist + SLO traces for HealthWave pilot

Thanks Monica — that was helpful. A couple quick clarifications:

- Can you confirm the p95 number above is measured at 1k tokens or at our typical 600-token median? What should we expect at 600 tokens?
- We will likely need an on-prem estimate for procurement. Can you provide a rough capacity/cost ballpark (GPUs and rack count) ahead of the deep-dive?

On the pilot: Tue 12/15 10:00 PT works for our engineers.

—Hannah

> Thanks again for the call earlier — great to learn more about HealthWave's triage and note-summarization workflow. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.
>

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Jenkins <hannah.jenkins@healthwave.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T18:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: model shortlist + SLO traces for HealthWave pilot

Hi Hannah,

Good questions — short answers below and attached a SLO trace visual (slo_trace_13b-quant.png).

- The p95 ~220 ms figure is from the RW-13B-quant profile measured at ~1k tokens; at 600 tokens we typically see p95 ~160–180 ms on the same hardware. I'll add a per-sequence-length table in the deep-dive.

- For an on-prem starting point (ballpark for your ~50 TPS target, replication for HA):
  - 2x A40 or A100-style nodes (shared across workloads) can hit ~40–60 TPS when configured with continuous batching and prefix caching. Rack/headcount depends on redundancy — we generally recommend 3 nodes for production HA.
  - I'll attach our rough calc (onprem_estimate_calc.xlsx) before procurement. Consider quantized 8-bit builds to reduce GPU memory and cost.

Pilot plan proposal (minimal):
- 2-week pilot using Redwood Dedicated sandbox
- Redwood runs benchmarks using your sample logs and our verified profile; we provide weekly summary of recall/latency and token cost
- Success check at end: quality regression <2% vs baseline AND p95 latency <= target you confirm

I've penciled Tue 12/15 10:00 PT for the deep-dive. Vivek/Ben — can you confirm availability?

Thanks,

Monica

Attachments: slo_trace_13b-quant.png (image)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Jenkins <hannah.jenkins@healthwave.ai>
Date: 2026-12-13T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: model shortlist + SLO traces for HealthWave pilot

Looping infra in and attaching the cost calc I promised. Ben/Monica: I'll run a quick sizing and update the spreadsheet (onprem_estimate_calc.xlsx) with dual-node and three-node HA options and estimated cost per month.

Hannah — initial quick note: for 600-token median and ~50 TPS, the 3-node HA cluster with A40s gives good headroom and keeps p95 under 200ms with continuous batching; we'll confirm numbers in the deep-dive.

-Vivek

Attachments: onprem_estimate_calc.xlsx (xlsx)
